Implement a small immutable state module for tracking maintenance tickets.

Export exactly `{ initialState, addTicket, toggleTicket, deleteTicket, ticketReducer }` using `module.exports`.

`initialState` must be the frozen object `{ nextId: 1, tickets: [] }`, with its empty `tickets` array also frozen.

Action creators:
- `addTicket(title, details)` returns `{ type: 'ticket/add', payload: { title, details } }`.
- `toggleTicket(id)` returns `{ type: 'ticket/toggle', payload: { id } }`.
- `deleteTicket(id)` returns `{ type: 'ticket/delete', payload: { id } }`.

`ticketReducer(state = initialState, action)` must:
- For `'ticket/add'`, require trimmed non-empty string `title` and string `details`; otherwise throw `TypeError`. Append `{ id, title: trimmedTitle, details, status: 'Open' }`, then increment `nextId`.
- For `'ticket/toggle'`, require a positive integer ID or throw `TypeError`. Toggle the matching ticket between `'Open'` and `'Resolved'`. If absent, return the original state object.
- For `'ticket/delete'`, require a positive integer ID or throw `TypeError`. Remove the match. If absent, return the original state object.
- For unknown or malformed actions, return the original state object.

Every actual change must return a new state, a new tickets array, and new objects only for tickets that changed. The reducer must never mutate its inputs. Ticket order is insertion order and IDs are never reused.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.

Implement a CommonJS module exporting exactly `{ mapSafely }`.

`mapSafely(values, mapper, fallback)` processes every numeric index of an array from `0` through `length - 1`, including sparse positions as `undefined`. `mapper(value, index)` produces the corresponding output value.

If `mapper` throws, append `{ index, error }` to an `errors` array and place a fallback value in the output. When `fallback` is a function, call it as `fallback(error, index, value)`; otherwise use it directly. Errors thrown by the fallback must propagate immediately.

Return `{ values, errors }`, preserving index order. Reject a non-array `values` or non-function `mapper` with `TypeError`. Empty arrays return two empty arrays. Do not mutate the input array, and do not clone values returned by callbacks.

messages.content:
Implement a framework-independent profile editor state machine. Export exactly `{ createEditorState, reduceEditor }` with `module.exports`.

`createEditorState()` takes no arguments and returns `{ phase: "idle", values: { name: "", description: "" }, saved: { name: "", description: "" }, error: null }`.

`reduceEditor(state, action)` must require both arguments to be non-null, non-array objects, otherwise throw `TypeError("Invalid editor input")`. It must support:
- `{ type: "load-start" }`: phase becomes `"loading"` and error becomes null.
- `{ type: "load-success", profile }`: `profile.name` and `profile.description` must be strings. Both `values` and `saved` become independent copies of those fields; phase becomes `"ready"`; error becomes null.
- `{ type: "edit", field, value }`: field must be `"name"` or `"description"`, and value must be a string. Update only that value and set phase to `"ready"`.
- `{ type: "save-start" }`: if `values.name.trim()` is empty, return phase `"error"` with error `"Name required"`. Otherwise return phase `"saving"` with no error.
- `{ type: "save-success" }`: copy current values into saved, set phase to `"ready"`, and clear the error.
- `{ type: "failure", message }`: message must be a non-empty string; set phase to `"error"` and store it.

An unsupported or malformed action must throw `TypeError("Invalid action")`. Neither the prior state nor action may be mutated. Every successful call must return a fresh top-level state, a fresh `values` object, and a fresh `saved` object, including when their contents do not change.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.

Implement `createTaskDispatcher()` and export exactly `{ createTaskDispatcher }` using `module.exports`. It returns a function `dispatch(request)` that synchronously processes an in-memory task collection. No HTTP or framework APIs are used.

A request must be a non-array object with string `method` and `path`; malformed requests return `{ status: 400, body: { error: "Bad request" } }`. Supported operations are:
- `GET /items`: return status 200 and all items in creation order.
- `POST /items`: `body.text` must be a non-empty string. Create `{ id: "iN", text }`, where N is a per-dispatcher counter starting at 1, and return it with status 201.
- `PUT /items/:id`: require a non-empty string `body.text`; replace the matching item's text and return it with status 200.
- `DELETE /items/:id`: remove the item and return `{ status: 204, body: null }`.

Paths must match exactly: empty IDs, extra slashes, query strings, and additional segments are unsupported and return status 404. A missing item returns `{ status: 404, body: { error: "Not found" } }`. An invalid POST or PUT body returns `{ status: 400, body: { error: "Text required" } }`. Other method/path combinations return `{ status: 404, body: { error: "Not found" } }`.

Requests and bodies must not be mutated or retained. Every returned item, array, and response body must be a fresh snapshot. Failed creation must not consume an ID. Dispatcher instances must have independent collections and counters.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.

Implement `createSignalHub()` and export an object containing exactly this function with `module.exports`.

The returned hub must expose `on(topic, handler)`, `off(topic, handler)`, and `publish(topic, payload)`. A topic is a non-empty string and a handler is a function; invalid arguments throw `TypeError`. Registering the same function twice for one topic is idempotent. `on` returns a zero-argument unsubscribe function. `off` returns whether the handler was present.

`publish` invokes handlers synchronously in registration order and returns the number invoked. It must use a snapshot: additions or removals made by a handler affect later publications, not the current one. Handler exceptions propagate immediately. Publishing an unregistered topic returns zero. Payloads are passed through unchanged, and the hub must never mutate them.

Implement a new framework-independent path matcher.

Export these declarations:

- `interface RouteSpec { readonly pattern: string; readonly destination: string }`
- `interface RouteMatch { readonly destination: string; readonly params: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }`
- `function matchPath(routes: readonly RouteSpec[], path: string): RouteMatch | null`

Paths and patterns must start with `/`, must not contain empty interior segments, and must not contain `?` or `#`; malformed values throw `TypeError`. A pattern segment is either a literal or a parameter beginning with `:` followed by a non-empty name. A pattern may instead be exactly `"*"`, which is the fallback. Duplicate parameter names within a pattern are invalid. The root pattern `/` matches only `/`.

Select the matching non-fallback route with the greatest number of literal segments. If specificity ties, use declaration order. Use the first fallback only when no ordinary route matches. Parameter values are raw path segments without decoding. Empty route arrays return `null`. Return a fresh parameter object and do not mutate or reorder the route array.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.

Implement a new function `decodeInlineNotes(input: string): InlinePart[]`. Export `InlinePart` as a discriminated union with `{ type: "text"; text: string }`, `{ type: "note" | "warning" | "key"; text: string }`, and `{ type: "route"; text: string; target: string }`. Recognize complete markers `{{note:payload}}`, `{{warning:payload}}`, `{{key:payload}}`, and `{{route:label|target}}`. A backslash escapes the next character both inside and outside markers and is removed from output; a trailing backslash represents a literal backslash. For routes, the first unescaped `|` separates label and target. Empty payloads and empty route fields are valid. Unknown, incomplete, or malformed markers are emitted as ordinary text. Markers do not nest. Return parts in source order, coalescing adjacent ordinary text into one part. Empty input returns an empty array and the function must not retain mutable state between calls.

Implement a new observable state container for three dashboard panels.

Export:
- `type PanelId = "map" | "metrics" | "notes"`
- `type PanelSnapshot = Readonly<Record<PanelId, boolean>>`
- class `PanelStateStore`

Its constructor accepts `Partial<Record<PanelId, boolean>>`, defaulting omitted panels to `false`. At runtime, an explicitly supplied non-boolean value must cause `TypeError`. The class exposes:
- `getSnapshot(): PanelSnapshot`
- `setVisible(id: PanelId, visible: boolean): void`
- `toggle(id: PanelId): void`
- `subscribe(listener: (snapshot: PanelSnapshot) => void): () => void`

Subscriptions are not called immediately. A listener is notified after every `setVisible` or `toggle`, even if `setVisible` repeats the current value. Notify listeners in subscription order using a snapshot of the listener list, so subscription changes during notification affect only later updates. The returned unsubscribe function is idempotent. Each notification and `getSnapshot` must receive a newly allocated frozen snapshot; no internal object may escape. Listener exceptions propagate and stop that notification pass.

Implement a new, standard-library-only TypeScript module exporting `BalanceListener` and `FixedScaleVault`.

Construct `FixedScaleVault(decimals: number, symbol: string)`. Decimals must be a safe integer from 0 through 18. The symbol and every account identifier must contain a non-whitespace character; valid strings remain exact and are case-sensitive.

Expose:
- `parseAmount(text: string): bigint`
- `formatAmount(units: bigint): string`
- `getBalance(account: string): bigint`
- `setBalance(account: string, units: bigint): void`
- `subscribe(account: string, listener: BalanceListener): () => void`
- `allowance(owner: string, spender: string): bigint`
- `approve(owner: string, spender: string, units: bigint): void`
- `getSymbol(): string`
- `getDecimals(): number`

Amounts are non-negative. `parseAmount` accepts only canonical unsigned decimal notation: an integer part of `0` or a nonzero digit followed by digits, and optionally a dot plus 1 through `decimals` digits. No sign, whitespace, separators, exponent, leading zeroes, or trailing dot is allowed. When decimals is zero, no dot is allowed. Missing fractional places are padded on the right. Throw `TypeError` for a non-string and `RangeError` for malformed or negative amounts. `formatAmount` emits a canonical string, omitting the decimal point when decimals is zero and otherwise always emitting exactly `decimals` fractional digits.

Unknown balances and allowances are zero. Setters reject non-bigint or negative values. Subscribers are called immediately with the current balance, then synchronously after each actual balance change. Duplicate-value assignments emit nothing. Listeners run in registration order from a snapshot of the listeners present when emission begins; subscription changes during a callback affect later emissions only. The returned function is idempotent. Listener exceptions propagate. Do not mutate caller-owned data.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
